subject.title: Bug: Gateway falsely marks healthy local vLLM endpoints as timed out/overloaded, causing 1–23 min fallback cascades

question: Is the current issue ready for an implementation PR, or should maintainers first require a fresh current-main local vLLM trace that isolates the remaining timeout and gateway RPC cascade?
rationale: Current source proves several adjacent slices were fixed, but the original healthy-vLLM false-timeout cascade still spans timeout policy, provider routing, auth-profile state, cron/live-session behavior, and gateway RPC latency without an end-to-end current-main reproduction.

options.title: Require current-main live trace
options.body: Capture the vLLM and Gateway timing evidence first, then choose the narrow code path to fix from the observed bottleneck.

options.title: Queue a speculative timeout fix
options.body: Start a repair from the timeout/fallback code now, accepting a higher risk of masking the wrong latency source.

options.title: Close after partial fixes only
options.body: Close only if a maintainer confirms current main no longer reproduces the false timeout and sessions_spawn cascade in a comparable local vLLM setup.

recommendation.title: Require current-main live trace
recommendation.body: Capture the vLLM and Gateway timing evidence first, then choose the narrow code path to fix from the observed bottleneck.

likelyOwner.reason: osolmaz is the current assignee and has recent merger/coordination history on the related cron and provider-auth slices.
